newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RANGERS SIGN RW KEANE, C SKRUDLAND TO MULTI-YEAR DEALS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RANGERS SIGN RW KEANE, C SKRUDLAND TO MULTI-YEAR DEALS.

text.p: The New York Rangers landed a pair of free agents Monday, signing checking specialists Mike Keane and Brian Skrudland to multi-year deals to add much-needed muscle to a lineup that was manhandled by the Philadelphia Flyers in the playoffs.
Financial terms were not disclosed, but published reports said that right wing Keane signed a four-year contract worth $8 million and Skrudland signed a three-year deal worth more than $5 million.

The two immediately provide the Rangers with the foundation of a strong veteran checking line to combat the top scoring lines in the NHL, such as Philadelphia's Legion of Doom line after Eric Lindros and John LeClair physically dominated New York in the Eastern Conference finals this year.
Keane and Skrudland will likely join with Bill Berg to form the Rangers' checking line for the 1997-1998 campaign.
The 30-year-old Keane was a member of Stanley Cup championship teams in Montreal and Colorado. He played the last two seasons with the Avalanche and had 10 goals and 17 assists last season.

The 33-year-old Skrudland had been the only captain in the history of the Florida Panthers. Skrudland, who is coming off knee surgery, was limited to 51 games last season and missed the playoffs. He had five goals and 13 assists in 1996-97.
